That reply often carries headers, for example `HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established\\r\\nProxy-agent: Squid\\r\\n\\r\\nHTTP/2 404 ...`. The new skip rule `(status < 200 || headers.is_empty()) && body.starts_with(\"HTTP/\")` does not skip that block: its status is 200 and it has a header. The parser then returns status 200 with the whole real response, status line included, as the body, so a real 404 or 429 is misread as 200 with an unparseable body. The old code took the last status line, so it handled this case, and the old doc comment promised it. No test covers a preamble that has headers.","fix":"Skip any block whose body starts with `HTTP/`, whatever its status or headers, with `if body.starts_with(\"HTTP/\") { rest = body; continue; }`. A JSON or HTML body never starts with a status line, and the condition gets simpler. Add one test with a CONNECT 200 preamble that has a `Proxy-agent` header, followed by a 404."},{"file":"crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/http.rs","issue":"The existing test `a_response_is_split_at_the_last_header_block_and_keeps_its_headers` is now misnamed.
